prespecification_note: Written and checksum-pinned before any dexamethasone curve, Cmax or AUC was computed. Not blinded: the label was read in full and one hand calculation was made: 20 mg / 1271 ng.h/mL = 15.7 L/h, equal to the stated CL/F. The rules mirror the pomalidomide plan (label-exposure-consistency-plan-v1.0), adapted to a label that reports single-dose values only.
not_this: Not validation: a label agreeing with itself says nothing about whether the curve describes patients.
Not an outside-data check; that would be a later step with its own locked plan.
Not a dosing recommendation or an exposure prediction for any patient.
question: Can a one-compartment, typical-value oral curve built from the HEMADY label by fixed rules reproduce the label's own single-dose statements, and may the engine use it?

inputs.population: The label's single-dose values are from 'subjects', not stated to be myeloma patients; every output says so.
inputs.regimen: One 20 mg oral dose. 40 mg is the same curve doubled (dose proportional 0.5-40 mg per the label). Once-daily dosing barely accumulates (about 1.6% of a dose remains at 24 h with a 4 h half-life), so the single-dose curve is the unit shown.

model.structure: One compartment, first-order absorption, no lag time, linear; apparent parameters (CL/F, V/F).
model.single_dose_concentration: C(t) = Dose ka / (V/F (ka - k)) (e^(-k t) - e^(-ka t)), k = (CL/F)/(V/F).
model.ka_rule: Derived from Tmax = ln(ka/k) / (ka - k), using the label's median Tmax of 1 h. Sensitivity: the label's Tmax range ends, 0.5 h and 4 h (individual extremes, reported only).
model.numerical: Cmax and Tmax on a 0.001 h grid over 48 h; AUC0-inf by trapezoids to 48 h plus C(48)/k, checked against Dose/CL.

parameter_set.cl_f: 15.7 L/h, the stated oral clearance after a single dose.
parameter_set.v_f: CL/F x t1/2 / ln 2, with t1/2 = 4 h (the label states no volume).
parameter_set.why_one_set: The label gives one clearance and one half-life, both from single doses; there is no second set to choose between. The stated clearance is used (not Dose/AUC) so that C1 and C4 are informative checks.

C1_clearance_vs_exposure.compare: CL/F 15.7 L/h against Dose / AUCinf (20 mg / 1271 ng.h/mL)

C2_half_life.compare: ln 2 x V/F / CL/F against 4 h

C3_single_dose_cmax.compare: Model Cmax after 20 mg against the geometric mean 247 ng/mL

C4_single_dose_auc.compare: Model AUC0-inf after 20 mg against the geometric mean 1271 ng.h/mL

C6_tmax.role: descriptive; set by the ka rule

checks.which_checks_are_informative: C2 holds by construction (V/F comes from the half-life) and the model Tmax equals 1 h by the ka rule. C1, C3 and C4 are informative.

tolerance.rule: A pass-or-fail check passes if model / label is within 0.67 to 1.5 inclusive.
tolerance.why: Same as the pomalidomide and melphalan plans. Comparing a typical-value curve with geometric means is appropriate: both describe a central value on the log scale.

decision_rule.selection: The engine may use set A if it passes C1 to C4 with ka from Tmax 1 h.
decision_rule.if_it_fails: Dexamethasone is recorded as not eligible for a label-based curve, with the failing checks.
decision_rule.never: No value is adjusted after seeing results.

scenarios.rule: Itraconazole (AUC x 3.7) and aprepitant (AUC x 2.2) are applied as CL/F divided by the fold, one at a time, with the dose and population each was studied at shown. The food effect changes Cmax but not AUC and is text only. No renal, hepatic or inducer scenario is offered: the label gives no numbers.
scenarios.not_checked_here: Scenarios are carried into the engine, not tested.
